item.title: Still colonised, still grateful for scraps
item.description: THE EDITOR: We are far more colonised than we care to admit. I remember working in administration at Petrotrin when a US citizen arrived to access the refinery for a meeting. He was driving on a US driver’s licence long past the lawful period allowed under TT law. I refused to process the request. What followed was instructive. item.title: Not making this a habit
item.description: THE EDITOR: I now fondly remember being in my teens and my father giving a lift to someone hitchhiking on the side of the road on evenings. Sometimes I pointed out someone and asked him to stop for them. We didn’t think of that as dangerous then. Fast forward a few decades. item.title: No joking matter
item.description: SEVENTEEN years since the Manning administration agreed to a bailout of the tottering CL Financial empire, no one has been held accountable. Throughout those years, taxpayers have borne a $28 billion burden, made heavier by staggering legal fees ­– $3 billion to $4 billion – in cases before the civil courts. item.title: Lifting of exchange controls one-sided
item.description: THE EDITOR: The selective lifting of the Exchange Control Act for international lenders, while leaving local citizens and businesses constrained, exposes a serious contradiction in national economic policy. item.title: National MMA Champs kicks off on January 31
item.description: The Trinidad and Tobago Mixed Martial Arts Federation (TT-MMAF) will stage the National Invitational MMA Championship on January 31 at the Woodbrook Youth Facility. The event represents a major development in the country’s continued growth as a regional leader in internationally sanctioned mixed martial arts. item.title: President Kangaloo pays tribute to Lionel Darceuil
item.description: PRESIDENT Christine Carla Kangaloo expressed heartfelt condolences on the passing of Lionel D’Arceuil, a distinguished table tennis player and revered national sporting icon. D’Arceuil was regarded as one of the country’s most accomplished and respected table tennis athletes. Over a career spanning several decades, he represented TT with distinction at the national, regional, and international levels, earning widespread admiration for his exceptional skill, discipline, and sportsmanship. item.description: THE EDITOR: As a young working woman I look forward to Carnival each year, but, like many others, I don’t always have a lot of disposable income to spend on fetes and events. item.description: LESTER PHILIP THE NEWS from Venezuela has been dramatic – US special forces stormed in, captured Nicolás Maduro, and Washington is already calling it a “big win.” Fast, clean, and surgical. item.title: Teacher disenchantment: Navigating uncertainty in 2025-2026
item.description: IN APRIL 2025, the TT Unified Teachers’ Association (TTUTA) formally signed off on salary negotiations on behalf of its membership. item.title: Trinidad and Tobago U-17 women marry mental health, on-field prep
item.description: As many as nine overseas-based players have been selected in Trinidad and Tobago's 21-member squad for the 2026 Concacaf Under-17 Women’s qualifiers, which will run from January 24 to February 1. TT will be in group F alongside Barbados, El Salvador and hosts Curacao, with Guadeloupe pulling out because of financial constraints.
